text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sarajevo press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Croat partner in the US-backed military aid programme is not satisfied with actual balance of power 70:30, in favour of Moslem side, sources tell newspaper. Croat side asks also that still-unloaded shipment of arms be shared 50-50 between them, says same source. Croatia also wants to impose taxes on arms passing through Croatian territory before reaching Bosnia.

- Deputy defence minister Hasan Cengic's former media adviser, Faris Nanic, says Cengic won't be sacked but promoted. He says it "was a kind of compromise" and will likely happen after new federal parliament is constituted.
- Bosnian federation government decided to finance immediate needs such as military pensions, police, education and health care with 30 million German marks.
- European Union envoy to Mostar Sir Martin Garrod again urged Bosnian Croats to stop expulsions of non-Croat population from Mostar.
- Bosnian Serbs released four Moslem prisoners on the inter entity boundary line in Sarajevo on Thursday. -Sarajevo newsroom, +387-71-663-864.
